question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}), & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(0.2<X<1).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $X$ for $0\le x\le 1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{2}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}y+\frac{1}{2}{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =[\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}]-0 \\  & =\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{X}(x)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}, & 0\le x\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.2<X<1) & ={\int }_{0.2}^{1}{f}_{X}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0.2}^{1}(\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{2})\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{2}x]}_{0.2}^{1} \\  & =[\frac{1}{2}(1)^{3}+\frac{1}{2}(1)]-[\frac{1}{2}(0.2)^{3}+\frac{1}{2}(0.2)] \\  & =1-0.104 \\  & =0.896.\end{aligned}
$$
